calls.why: I trust the movement and the rep target, not the number: 205 was set on the old gym's smith machine, whose bar counterweight is baked into that figure, and on 2026-09-03 the same-name machine at the new gym read 77-88 where the old one read 127.5, so carried loads are not comparable. He also only completed 3 of 4 sets on 2026-08-16 and missed the 8-10 target on the first set, so there was nothing to push even before the move; this re-enters at a load he can verify on whatever bar is actually there.

Repeat is right for the wrong reason and still right: on 2026-08-16 he went 12, 11, 10 at 180, which is a failed set-three, so no increase was earned. Trust the 180 only as an old-building stack position, since a leg press at the new gym may be plate-loaded or scaled differently; the honest instruction here is the 3x10-12 target, and the weight is whatever gets him there.

He genuinely earned a jump: 142.5 for 12, 12, 12, 12 on 2026-08-16 and 142.5x13 twice on 2026-08-20, both topping the range. But 150 is a pin slot on a machine he no longer uses, and the app's progression would put him on an unverified stack at a number he has never touched anywhere. I trust the effort level, not the 142.5, so I hold rather than push and let the first set at the new gym re-establish the scale.

The app's cross would prescribe 135x15, a rep count he has not hit; on 2026-08-20 both sets stopped at 13, mid-range. Trust the 13-rep ceiling, not the 135 itself, because that plate number belongs to the old gym's abductor stack and this was three weeks ago.

105 for 12 and 12 on 2026-08-20 sits at the bottom of the 12-15 window, so nothing was earned even on the old machine. I trust the rep result fully and the 105 not at all until he has seen the new gym's adductor stack once.

The app would print 300x15 three times, a number he has never once produced: 12, 12, 12 on 2026-08-16 and 13, 13, 12 on 2026-08-20. I am correcting the rep target down to what he has actually done. The 300 is a calf-press reading off the old leg press and carries none of my confidence at a new machine.

60x12 x3 on 2026-08-16 then 60x13 x3 on 2026-08-20 is a clean earn, so on the old cable stack 65 would be correct. Cables are exactly where the gym change bites hardest, though: his close-grip pulldown moved from 127.5 to 77-88 on 2026-09-03, so a cable pin number is the least transferable figure in this session. Holding at 60 means the first set measures the new stack instead of guessing at it.

This is the only slot today I trust completely: bodyweight carries between buildings, so nothing here was invalidated by the move. He did 12, 12 on 2026-08-16 and 13, 12 on 2026-08-20, climbing inside the 12-15 window, so one more rep on each set is the real progression while the loaded lifts wait for their scales to be re-established.
